mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI engine costs £2,800-£4,500 supply-only, or £3,500-£6,000 fully fitted depending on engine code (CUNA, CRLB, DFGA) and supplier location. Used engines start around £1,200 but carry higher risk. CUNA (2012-2016, 150hp): £2,800-£4,500 reconditioned. CRLB (2016-2020, 184hp): £2,800-£4,500 reconditioned. DFGA (2020+, 35 TDI): £2,800-£4,500 reconditioned.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector failure in an Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include rough idle, excessive smoke on startup, loss of power, and visible carbon buildup around injector bases ("Black Death"). You may also notice increased fuel consumption and difficulty starting when cold. Black carbon deposits around injectors indicate seal failure. Knocking or rattling noise suggests injector mechanical wear. ECU fault codes for cylinder balance or injector circuit.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: For 8V generation cars (2012-2020) valued £8,000-£18,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,500 typically represents good value if you plan to keep the car 2+ years. For older 8P models under £5,000, a used engine may be more economical. 8P (2003-2012): Usually worth under £5k; used engine often better value. 8V (2012-2020): Worth £8k-£18k; rebuilt engine justified for most owners. 8Y (2020+): Worth £14k-£28k; rebuilt engine is small percentage of value.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete engine swap typically takes 1-2 days for supply-and-fit service, depending on supplier workload and whether additional components (turbo, injectors, DPF) need replacement. Supply-only delivery takes 2-5 working days nationwide. Simple swap (good condition peripherals): 1 day. Complex swap (turbo/DPF/injector work): 1.5-2 days. Diagnostics and ECU coding: Additional 2-4 hours.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 2.0 TDI and 35 TDI in the Audi A3?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 35 TDI is the WLTP naming convention introduced in 2020 for the 150hp 2.0 TDI engine (DFGA code). Mechanically, it's the same EA288 Evo engine family as the CUNA, just with updated emissions systems and mild-hybrid capability on some 8Y models. 2.0 TDI (CUNA/CRLB): 2012-2020, 150hp or 184hp, pre-WLTP naming. 35 TDI (DFGA): 2020-present, 150hp, WLTP naming, Euro 6d compliance. Engine codes differ but core architecture remains EA288 2.0L diesel.

mainEntity.name: Are reconditioned Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI engines reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, reconditioned 2.0 TDI engines from our specialists include upgraded components addressing known failure points like injector seals, timing chain tensioners, and oil pump wear. With proper maintenance, a quality reconditioned unit should last 80k-120k miles. All rebuilt engines include minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Upgraded parts address original design weaknesses. Specialist rebuilders test compression and oil pressure before dispatch.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 2.0 TDI badge has been the workhorse diesel option in the A3 range since the 8P generation, evolving through multiple engine codes and power outputs before becoming the 35 TDI under WLTP naming in 2020.

milestones.description: 8P generation launches with 2.0 TDI (140hp), BMN/BMM engine codes, PD (Pumpe Düse) unit injector system
Common rail 2.0 TDI introduced (140hp), CFFB engine code, replacing PD system for Euro 5 compliance
8V generation debuts with EA288 2.0 TDI (150hp), CUNA engine code, improved efficiency and lower emissions
8V facelift adds 2.0 TDI (184hp), CRLB engine code, for buyers seeking stronger performance
8Y generation launches with WLTP naming: 35 TDI (150hp), DFGA engine code, mild-hybrid options introduced
8Y continues with refined DFGA and updated emissions systems for Euro 6d-ISC-FCM compliance

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: Injector Failure & Carbon Buildup - Why the Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI EA288 Develops "Black Death"
problems.affectedModels: Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI (CUNA, CRLB, DFGA, 2012-present)
problems.rootCause: Diesel injector seals degrade over time, allowing fuel to leak and create carbon deposits around the injector base ("Black Death"), eventually causing injector failure and compression loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, replace copper washers and seals, clean carbon buildup
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix if caught early; doesn't address worn injectors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace one failed injector, code to ECU, clean surrounding area
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one injector failed and others test good

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded injectors and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when multiple injectors failed or severe carbon damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI from 2012-2016 (CUNA) is worth £5,000-£12,000; 2016-2020 (CRLB) £8,000-£18,000; 2020+ (DFGA/35 TDI) £14,000-£28,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader UK 2025 data]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: injector repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If carbon buildup is caught early with minimal compression loss, injector seal replacement can extend life 12-24 months. However, once "Black Death" is visible or multiple injectors fail, a rebuilt engine with upgraded seals is more cost-effective than piecemeal repairs that risk recurring failure.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CUNA/CRLB/DFGA Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: DPF & EGR System Failure - Why the Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI Chokes on Urban Driving
problems.affectedModels: Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI (CUNA, CRLB, DFGA, all EA288 variants, 2012-present)
problems.rootCause: Short-trip urban driving prevents DPF regeneration cycles, causing soot buildup that eventually blocks the filter and forces EGR valve into constant recirculation, reducing power and increasing emissions.

repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix if filter not physically damaged; doesn't address root cause

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New DPF unit, EGR valve cleaning/replacement, ECU reset
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if engine otherwise healthy and driving patterns will change

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit with updated emissions components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best when DPF failure caused secondary damage (turbo contamination, oil dilution)

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See values above. Most affected 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI cars are 8V generation (2012-2020) valued £8k-£18k, placing them in the "reconditioned viable" to "rebuilt justified" range depending on condition and ownership horizon.
problems.recommendation: If the DPF failed due to driving patterns that won't change (e.g., you still do mostly short urban trips), even a new DPF will clog again. A rebuilt engine won't solve this unless you also address usage patterns. However, if DPF blockage caused turbo damage or severe oil dilution, replacement is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CUNA/CRLB/DFGA Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Wear & Oil Contamination - Why the Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI Loses Boost
problems.affectedModels: Audi A3 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI (CUNA, CRLB, DFGA, 2012-present, especially high-mileage examples)
problems.rootCause: Turbocharger bearing wear from extended oil change intervals or DPF regeneration fuel dilution reduces oil viscosity, causing premature turbo failure and potential metal contamination throughout the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove old turbo, fit new/recon unit, oil/fluid flush
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if turbo failed cleanly with no metal debris in oil

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbo replacement plus complete oil system clean, cooler flush
repairOptions.longevity: Better option but still risky if metal debris circulated

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit with new turbo, upgraded oil pump, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Safest option when turbo failed catastrophically or metal debris confirmed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See values above. Given most 2.0 TDI / 35 TDI cars with turbo failure are valued £8k-£18k, a rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,500 represents 25-40% of vehicle value - typically justified for owners planning 2+ years of continued use.
problems.recommendation: Never replace a turbo on a 2.0 TDI without confirming oil contamination levels. If metal debris is present (check sump plug and oil filter), a turbo-only replacement will fail quickly as debris circulates. A rebuilt engine with fresh oil galleries is the only reliable fix in these cases.
